From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Emily Choe <emily.choe@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - perf targets + hardware questions

Rishi / Ben / Emily —

Quick status update from the lab runs this morning. Attached: perf-results-20260219.csv (summary rows below). Full raw traces uploaded to the shared drive link in the MAP draft.

Summary (avg prompt 120 tokens):
- H100 (full GPU): p95 latency = 140ms @ concurrency 8, throughput = ~1.2k tokens/sec, TTFT = 18ms, effective batch = 16
- A100-80GB (full): p95 latency = 165ms @ concurrency 8, throughput = ~1.0k tokens/sec, TTFT = 22ms
- L40S (full): p95 latency = 210ms @ concurrency 8, throughput = ~0.85k tokens/sec, TTFT = 26ms
- H100 (4-way MIG, equal partitions): p95 latency = 190ms @ concurrency 16 (distributed), throughput per MIG ~0.4k tokens/sec, aggregate throughput comparable to 1 full GPU but with higher p95
- A100 MIG: similar trend; per-MIG throughput smaller and p95 degraded ~20-30% vs full GPU at same aggregate concurrency.

Notes:
- TTFT improvements on H100 are visible due to kernel-level fusions for attention; warm KV cache reduced TTFT by ~5-8ms in steady state.
- For our model family (decoder-only transformer ~7B), memory footprints allow multiple model instances per A100-80 but fewer on 40GB.

Prelim sizing for Acme pilot (10k MAU, peak concurrency estimated 150 concurrent requests):
- Option A (latency-first): 6 x H100 full GPUs (expected to meet p95 < 200ms with horizontal headroom for spikes).
- Option B (cost-balanced): 10 x A100-80GB full GPUs or 18 x L40S full GPUs (cheaper per-hour trades off latency).
- Option C (dense packing, cost-min): MIG strategy ~24 x A100-40 partitions — cheaper but p95 risk; recommend only for non-latency-critical background workloads.

I’ll push the CSV + a short one-pager into the MAP draft. Rishi — I kept the pricing buckets in the spreadsheet at list rates; we can adjust to proposed committed pricing for the deal.

Marissa
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: perf-results-20260219.csv (csv)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Choe <emily.choe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: [MAP v1] Performance appendix + sizing recommendation (A100/H100/L40S)

Emily —

Attached is MAP_Acme_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones, acceptance criteria, and perf appendix) and a one-page PDF summary (gpu-sizing-recs.pdf). Highlights:

- Acceptance criteria (example): p95 < 200ms and TTFT < 30ms at 150 concurrent sustained requests for pilot traffic profile; 99% availability during business hours for the first 90 days.
- Benchmarks: use Marissa's CSV as source of truth; the MAP appendix has a condensed table showing p50/p95/p99, TTFT, tokens/sec, and cost/hr for each config.
- Recommendation: For Acme's pilot (latency-sensitive primary path) we recommend the latency-first Option A (6x H100 full GPUs). That delivers p95 headroom and simpler operational model (no MIG fragmentation).
- Cost note: switching to committed dedicated pricing reduces the hourly delta vs A100 by ~18% in our estimate; I've included a committed pricing scenario in the MAP.
- Rollout plan: canary on 1 H100 with traffic shadowing (2 weeks), then scale to 3 H100, then cross-region standby (if required) before full 6-GPU pilot.

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm the acceptance criteria in the MAP spreadsheet (highlighted cells).
2) Procurement reviews the committed pricing bucket; we convert numbers to a SOW once price band accepted.
3) We schedule a 30-min alignment call Monday to lock the timeline for provisioning (I proposed 02/26 as procurement cutoff in the MAP).

If you prefer a cost-first approach we can pivot and re-run a small set of A100-80 vs L40S sizing tests with committed pricing to tighten the cost band.

Rishi
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
